lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: assembling transcripts, records, and references

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic assembling transcripts, records, and references task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Working from a provided fictional applicant's partially-completed document checklist, the learner figures out what is still missing, decides who that fictional applicant would need to contact for each item, and drafts the actual request message for two of the missing documents.
safetyNotes: All names, schools, and records in this lesson are fictional and provided; the learner does not enter or reference their own real transcript, grades, or personal records to complete it.
materials: learner-local: paper or notes app for drafting requests

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which part of drafting Jordan's requests (deciding who to ask, giving enough lead time, or including a helpful detail) do you think will be hardest for you to do for your own applications, and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement. | Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail. | Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a third missing item to Jordan's checklist (something not mentioned in the original profile, like standardized test scores or a portfolio) and draft the request message for it, including how it would change the lead-time plan.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic assembling transcripts, records, and references task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or notes app for drafting requests
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Working from a provided fictional applicant's partially-completed document checklist, the learner figures out what is still missing, decides who that fictional applicant would need to contact for each item, and drafts the actual request message for two of the missing documents.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact assembling transcripts, records, and references decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the fictional applicant's profile: Jordan Ellis is applying to a program with a deadline in six weeks.
Model move 3: For each missing or incomplete item, decide who Jordan would realistically need to contact to get it moving, and how much lead time that item typically needs.

Model check: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement. | Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail. | Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for assembling transcripts, records, and references.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Working from a provided fictional applicant's partially-completed document checklist, the learner figures out what is still missing, decides who that fictional applicant would need to contact for each item, and drafts the actual request message for two of the missing documents.
Coach direction: Read the fictional applicant's profile: Jordan Ellis is applying to a program with a deadline in six weeks.
Learner prompt: Based on Jordan's checklist, what is missing or incomplete right now?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each missing or incomplete item, decide who Jordan would realistically need to contact to get it moving, and how much lead time that item typically needs.

Response 1 (t2-p1): For the missing second reference, who would Jordan most likely ask (by role, e.g. a teacher, a supervisor, a coach), and how many weeks of lead time should Jordan give that person before the deadline?
Response 2 (t2-p2): My answer explains why that role is a reasonable person to ask, not just names a role.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Which part of drafting Jordan's requests (deciding who to ask, giving enough lead time, or including a helpful detail) do you think will be hardest for you to do for your own applications, and why?

Success checks: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement. | Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail. | Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional assembling transcripts, records, and references condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement. | Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail. | Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: Working from a provided fictional applicant's partially-completed document checklist, the learner figures out what is still missing, decides who that fictional applicant would need to contact for each item, and drafts the actual request message for two of the missing documents.

coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement.

simulationRoute.title: assembling transcripts, records, and references — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the assembling transcripts, records, and references task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which part of drafting Jordan's requests (deciding who to ask, giving enough lead time, or including a helpful detail) do you think will be hardest for you to do for your own applications, and why?
observableCriteria: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement.
Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail.
Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Gap identification: Warm-up correctly identifies both the missing second reference and the not-started personal statement. | Request message quality: Both drafted messages include a clear deadline and at least one specific, useful detail. | Self-application honesty: Reflection names one specific part of the process as hardest and gives a real reason.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
